---

Every reference in this register is a real, published document. **No IS clause
number, MES item number, SOR or SSR reference, specification number or document
title has been invented.**

Where a reference is carried over from master Part G it is marked `[C] master
Part G` — that register was compiled with the same rule and states that no clause
number in it was invented.

Where an exact reference could not be verified from the material available, the
entry says so in these words: *To be verified against the applicable MES SOR/SSR/specification edition.*

### How the register is used

* The **structural design** references govern what the structure is. They are the
  designer's, not the contractor's, and are reproduced here so that the Works
  Management documents cite the same authority as the design.
* The **construction, materials and workmanship** references govern how it is
  built and how it is accepted. These are the ones that appear in the inspection
  and test plan.
* The **measurement** references govern how the BOQ is measured and how the work
  is paid for.
* The **government** references — MES SSR, DWP, MESR, CPWD — govern the contract.
  Their existence is certain; their clause and item numbers are not, and none is
  quoted.

## MES, CPWD and Service specifications — the honest position

The Military Engineer Services **Standard Schedule of Rates** and the **Defence
Works Procedure** are the documents that would actually govern a Service work of
this kind. They exist, they are named correctly above, and the work they would
govern is identified.

What is **not** given is any item number, clause number or rate. None could be
verified from the material available in this project, and inventing one would put a
false authority on a document that an examiner or an executing engineer might rely
on. Every such entry therefore carries the words:

> *To be verified against the applicable MES SOR/SSR/specification edition.*

The same applies to the CPWD Specifications and the Delhi Schedule of Rates. The
documents are real and the editions named are real; the individual item numbers are
not quoted because they are not verified.
